newsitem.title: USA: USDA proposes compensation for wheat seed growers.
newsitem.headline: USDA proposes compensation for wheat seed growers.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department said Tuesday it was offering compensation to seed growers, seed companies and straw producers who lost money in 1995/96 because of karnal bunt regulations.
In an announcement, USDA said it would make up for lost value of seed wheat and straw.

"This will reduce the economic impact that growers and seed companies incurred due to karnal bunt regulations," said Alfred Elder, a deputy administrator of USDA's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service.

During the 1995-96 crop season, commercial shipments of wheat for seed were prohibited from leaving quarantined areas of Arizona, California, New Mexico and Texas. The rules prevented most of the seed wheat from reaching intended markets. It could be sold, at lower prices, for milling or feed.

USDA estimated 1.5 million bushels of seed wheat in the regulated areas sustained a loss from $5 million to $6 million. The department said it would pay eligible growers the difference between the selling price and the likely price for seed.
Seed companies were offered the same rate of compensation.
Straw growers who produced wheat straw under contract also would be eligible for compensation.

Claims for compensation would have to be filed within 60 days of the USDA offer becoming final. It was scheduled to appear in the Federal Register on Wednesday and be open to public comment until August 29.

Karnal bunt is a fungus that reduces yields and can produce an unpleasant odor and taste in flour made with heavily infected wheat. The fungus was detected in the United States in Arizona in March 1996 and jeopardized U.S. wheat exports.
